disclaimer: Advisory only. Always follow the product label and consult your local agriculture officer (Krishi Vigyan Kendra) before using any chemical.
sources: TNAU Agritech Portal – Tomato crop protection (agritech.tnau.ac.in)
ICAR – Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, tomato disease management (iihr.res.in)
University of California IPM – Tomato pest management guidelines (ipm.ucanr.edu)

symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves, often with a yellow halo
Spots merge and leaves turn yellow and drop
Raised scabby spots on fruit
Bacterial_spot.spread: Infected seed and plant debris; spreads by rain splash and overhead irrigation in warm, wet weather.
organic_control: Avoid overhead watering; water at the base
chemical_control: Copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride, often combined with mancozeb
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Crop rotation of 2–3 years away from tomato, pepper and eggplant
Do not work in the field when plants are wet

symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-like) on older, lower leaves
Yellowing around the spots
Leaves dry and fall, starting from the bottom of the plant
Early_blight.spread: Fungus survives in soil and plant debris; spread by wind and rain splash; favoured by warm, humid weather.
organic_control: Mulch the soil to stop spores splashing onto leaves
Bio-fungicides based on Trichoderma or Bacillus subtilis
chemical_control: Azoxystrobin (rotate with other groups to avoid resistance)
prevention: Wide spacing and staking for air flow
Balanced fertiliser (weak plants are more affected)

symptoms: Large, irregular, greasy grey-green to brown patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves in humid conditions
Brown, firm rot on fruit; whole plants can collapse within days
Late_blight.spread: Spores spread quickly by wind and rain in cool, wet weather; can destroy a field in a week.
organic_control: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)
prevention: Do not plant near potato fields
Spray protectively when cool, wet weather is forecast

symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mould on the underside
Mostly in greenhouses and polyhouses
Leaf_Mold.spread: Spreads in high humidity (above about 85%) and poor ventilation.

symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark brown edges and grey-white centres
Tiny black dots in the spot centres
Starts on lower leaves; heavy leaf loss
Septoria_leaf_spot.spread: Survives on plant debris and weeds; spread by rain splash, tools and hands in wet weather.

symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckles (stippling) on leaves
Fine webbing on the underside of leaves
Leaves turn bronze, dry and fall
Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider_mite.spread: Builds up fast in hot, dry, dusty conditions; often worse after broad-spectrum insecticide sprays kill natural predators.
organic_control: Strong water spray on the underside of leaves
chemical_control: Miticides such as abamectin or spiromesifen (rotate products to avoid resistance)

symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and concentric rings
Spots can merge and cause leaf drop
Sunken spots on fruit
Target_Spot.spread: Survives on plant debris; favoured by warm, humid weather and long leaf wetness.

symptoms: Leaves curl upwards and become small and yellow at the edges
Plants are stunted and bushy
Flowers drop and very few fruits form
Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.spread: Carried from plant to plant by whiteflies. There is no cure once a plant is infected.
organic_control: Uproot and destroy infected plants early
chemical_control: Whitefly control only (the virus itself cannot be treated): insecticides such as imidacloprid, thiamethoxam or spiromesifen, used according to local recommendations
prevention: Avoid planting next to old infected crops

symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves
Leaves are curled, wrinkled or fern-like
Stunted growth and uneven fruit ripening
Tomato_mosaic_virus.spread: Spreads by touch: hands, tools, clothes and infected seed. Very stable; survives in plant debris. No cure.
organic_control: Wash hands and disinfect tools between plants
No smoking or tobacco use near plants
chemical_control: No chemical cure; control relies on hygiene and resistant varieties

symptoms: No disease symptoms detected
prevention: Keep inspecting plants weekly, especially lower leaves
Water at the base, not over the leaves
Keep good spacing and remove weeds
